subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a disabled-by-default trusted-owner mode that bypasses approval prompts for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should it be a shared approval/elevated policy rather than a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: The request changes who can skip an approval gate for privileged actions and adds new config semantics, which automation cannot safely define without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy first
options.body: Define the bypass as a cross-channel approval/elevated policy with explicit group, sender, tool-class, destructive-op, and audit semantics before implementation.

options.title: Keep current approval prompts
options.body: Decline bypass semantics and keep trusted owners as approvers who can resolve prompts but cannot skip them in Telegram groups.

options.title: Prototype Telegram-only opt-in
options.body: Allow a narrow disabled-by-default Telegram setting, accepting the risk of channel-specific approval policy drift.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy first
recommendation.body: Define the bypass as a cross-channel approval/elevated policy with explicit group, sender, tool-class, destructive-op, and audit semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on elevated execution and security policy, and this owner has the strongest recent evidence in the relevant docs and policy surface.
